rationale: Typically an EPS-driven switch — risperidone's moderate EPS burden (especially above 4 mg) prompts a move to olanzapine's lower EPS profile. Introduce olanzapine first and stabilise at target before tapering risperidone, to avoid a window of sub-therapeutic cover. Counsel the patient that metabolic risk increases with olanzapine — weight, glucose and lipid monitoring is mandatory. Cholinergic and histaminergic effects of olanzapine will produce sedation initially; dose at night. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start olanzapine 5 mg nocte. Continue risperidone 4 mg. Warn patient about initial sedation and weight gain trajectory.
Increase olanzapine to 10 mg nocte (target dose). Hold risperidone 4 mg — allow olanzapine to stabilise before tapering.
Begin tapering risperidone: reduce to 3 mg. Olanzapine at steady state, antipsychotic cover maintained.
Reduce risperidone to 2 mg. Prolactin will begin to normalise as risperidone withdraws — counsel accordingly.
Reduce risperidone to 1 mg. Watch for any emergence of psychotic symptoms at this low dose.
Stop risperidone. Continue olanzapine 10 mg. Establish baseline weight, fasting glucose and lipids if not done at switch initiation.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Approximate clinical equivalency: risperidone 4 mg ≈ olanzapine 10 mg (Maudsley 15th, AP dose-equivalence table). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
